segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I ask, then: has God rejected his people? By no means! For I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars; I alone am left, and they are seeking my life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But what does the divine answer say to him?

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the same way, then, at the present time also there has come to be a remnant, chosen by grace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What then? What Israel is seeking, it did not obtain. The chosen obtained it, but the rest were hardened,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: just as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, to this very day.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And David says:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Let their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them;

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and keep their backs bent continually.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I ask, then: did they stumble so as to fall? By no means! Rather, through their misstep salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now if their misstep means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness mean!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I make much of my service,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: in the hope that I may somehow make my own flesh and blood jealous and save some of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if their casting aside means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If the firstfruits are holy, so is the whole batch of dough; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and came to share with them in the rich root of the olive tree,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root that supports you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You will say, then,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: True enough. They were broken off for lack of faith, and you stand by faith. Do not think highly of yourself, but be afraid;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Consider, then, the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God’s kindness toward you, provided you continue in his kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they too, if they do not continue in their lack of faith, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For I do not want you to be unaware of this secret, brothers and sisters, so that you will not be wise in your own eyes: a hardening has come upon Israel in part, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And this will be my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As regards the good news, they are enemies for your sake; but as regards God’s choice, they are beloved for the sake of their ancestors.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For just as you were once disobedient to God but have now received mercy through their disobedience,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so these too have now been disobedient, so that through the mercy shown to you they too may now receive mercy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For God has shut all people up in disobedience so that he may have mercy on all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Oh, the depth of the riches and the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Or

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “who has given to him first, so that he must be repaid?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever. Amen.

notes.note: The Greek says simply “in Elijah.” Before chapter and verse numbers existed, a passage of Scripture was located by naming its subject. The reference is to the story in 1 Kings 19, where Elijah complains to God about Israel and receives the reply quoted in verse 4.

notes.traditional: according to the election of grace
notes.note: The Greek noun means a choosing or selection. The traditional “election” is accurate as a theological term but now suggests voting, so the word is rendered with “choice” and “chosen” here and in verses 7 and 28. In verse 7 the abstract noun stands for the people chosen.

The word ordinarily means a wrongful act, and most versions have “trespass” or “transgression” here. Paul sets it directly beside “stumble” and “fall,” so the picture of a false step is active, and “misstep” keeps that picture while still naming a real failure. Some versions have “stumbling” for the same reason.

The Greek word means “nations” or “peoples,” and in the plural it is the regular Jewish term for the non-Jewish peoples. English versions render the same word as “Gentiles” or “nations” according to context; throughout this chapter it refers to non-Jews as distinct from Israel.

The word can mean a full number, a completion, or a state of fullness. Many interpreters take it here, and in verse 25 of the Gentiles, as the full number of those who will come in; others take it as Israel’s full restoration in contrast to its present “loss.” The rendering “fullness” leaves both open and keeps the two verses linked.

Most translations have “ministry.” The Greek was an everyday word for service or for a task carried out on someone’s behalf, and it did not denote a religious office. “Service” avoids the modern suggestion of a clerical profession; here it refers to Paul’s commission as apostle to the Gentiles.

The phrase most likely means God’s setting Israel aside for a time, balanced by his “acceptance” of them later; this is the majority view. Some scholars read it as Israel’s own rejection of the good news. The word differs from the verb in verses 1–2, where Paul denies that God has rejected his people, so a different English word is used here.

Numbers 15:17–21 instructs Israel to offer to God a portion from the first of its dough. Paul’s point is that the dedicated portion makes the whole batch holy. The firstfruits and the root are usually understood as the patriarchs, though some take the firstfruits to be the present remnant of Jewish believers.

notes.phrase: the rich root of the olive tree
notes.traditional: the root and fatness of the olive tree
notes.note: The text translated reads literally “the root of the richness of the olive tree.” Many later manuscripts read “the root and the richness,” which older English versions follow, and a few omit “the root.” The sense is little affected: the grafted branch draws on the nourishing sap of the tree.

Most English versions keep “mystery.” In Jewish Greek of the period the word was the ordinary term for a secret, especially a plan of God that only he can disclose. English “mystery” suggests a puzzle beyond understanding, whereas Paul goes on to state the content plainly.

notes.phrase: and in this way all Israel will be saved
notes.traditional: and so all Israel shall be saved
notes.note: The Greek expression normally indicates manner (“in this way”), pointing back to the process just described; some read it as temporal (“and then”). “All Israel” is also disputed: most scholars take it as the Jewish people as a whole, not necessarily every individual, while others take it as the elect of Israel through history or as the whole people of God, Jew and Gentile together.

The traditional rendering is “gospel,” which is now a religious term or a book title. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news. Many modern translations alternate between the two.

notes.phrase: through the mercy shown to you
notes.traditional: that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy
notes.note: In the Greek the words “the mercy shown to you” stand before “so that,” and they can be attached either way. Taken with what follows, as here and in most versions, they give the means by which Israel will receive mercy. Taken with what precedes, the sense is “they have now been disobedient for the sake of the mercy shown to you,” which parallels verse 30 more closely.

candidates.reason: Recurs in Romans 9–11, 1 Thessalonians and 2 Peter; translators split between “election” and “choice,” and the related ἐκλεκτός and ἐκλέγομαι need to match.
The plural address to mixed congregations occurs throughout the letters and Acts, and versions vary between “brothers,” “brothers and sisters” and “brethren.”
Paul’s formula of emphatic denial recurs across Romans, 1 Corinthians and Galatians and should be rendered identically everywhere.
Used in Romans, Ephesians, Colossians and John with disputed senses (full number, completeness, fullness), and readers would be misled by unexplained variation.
The figurative use for offspring recurs in Romans, Galatians, Hebrews and the Gospels, where “seed,” “offspring” and “descendants” compete and Galatians 3:16 turns on the singular.
